I am reviewing the current Monopoly game state to determine my next move.

I have three hotels and two get-out-of-jail cards. The opponent has almost no cash and only three houses on two properties. I am deciding whether to trade or build.

I am weighing the trade-off between selling my hotels and keeping them for rent. Unmortgaging the railroads would be a poor investment without a full set. I also need to avoid giving away Tennessee Avenue or cash, since that would help the opponent rebuild.

Virginia Avenue hotel rent is $900. I am checking the board order to see if the opponent's Indiana Avenue position falls before or after my pink hotels.

The opponent must pass GO before reaching the pink hotels. I am on Pacific Avenue, so I could land on Park Place or Boardwalk next.

I calculated the exact rent for Park Place and Boardwalk with three houses. Both are well within my cash range. I am now questioning whether to change my previous strategy of ending the turn without trading or building.

I considered trading for the opponent's dark blue properties to eliminate their income and potentially bankrupt them instantly. They would not give up those assets, so that path is closed. I am now looking for a trade offer that hurts them without giving away anything valuable.

Unmortgaging the Pennsylvania Railroad would cost $110 but only yield $25 in rent. Trading Tennessee Avenue to the opponent would complete their orange monopoly, which is a clear liability.

Unmortgaging Tennessee Avenue would cost $99 for only $14 in rent. The opponent is too far away to make it worthwhile. I will end my turn.
